terminal_reason: Self-correcting going forward: every PR opened by this lane from this point on will pass draft: false. The two already-open self-land PRs this bug affected (#14299, #14322) were un-drafted via update_pull_request and each needs one fresh push to its claude/* branch (claude-pr-automerge.yml triggers on `push`, not `ready_for_review`) before the relay re-evaluates and arms; #14332 (Tier-3 HELD) was un-drafted too, for consistency with the ruling, though HELD PRs don't need the relay to fire.
what: [process][pr-mechanics] Every PR this lane opened this session (#14051, #14053, #14299, #14322, #14332) was created with draft: true. That is WRONG for this repo: `.github/workflows/pr-opener.yml`'s own header states the `draft` default FLIPPED TO false on 2026-09-03 BY OPERATOR RULING -- "Going into github to marke drafts ready is not something we can include in the workflow" -- a draft is a hold its own author cannot lift (a sub-session 403s on update_pull_request), so every draft becomes a manual click for someone else. A PR is meant to be held by its LANDING DECLARATION (.github/pr-landing/<slug>.json, enforced by check_pr_landing.py), never by the draft flag, which is pure UI state. IMPACT, discovered while chasing why #14299 (Tier-1, self-land, CI green, mergeable_state clean) sat unmerged for over an hour: read the open-and-automerge job's own log (job 109518691631) -- it explicitly REFUSED to arm: "#14299 is a DRAFT this workflow did not open. ... Open the PR ready (pr-opener's draft: false) or ask the manager to merge it." The relay distrusts a draft opened by anything other than itself, by design -- correctly, since this session's own draft:true habit is exactly the failure mode that ruling was written to prevent. FIX APPLIED: update_pull_request(draft=false) on #14053, #14299, #14322, #14332 (#14051 could not be -- it is CLOSED, unrelated to this bug, see below). REMAINING WORK: claude-pr-automerge.yml triggers on `push` to claude/**, not on `ready_for_review`, so un-drafting alone does not re-arm #14299/#14322 -- each needs one more real push (this commit is that push for #14299; #14322 needs its own). SEPARATE, UNRELATED FINDING surfaced during the same check: #14051 (strip xrp_pullback_2h's trail_decay arm, Tier-3 HELD) is not open at all -- it was CLOSED 2026-09-29T10:05:20Z, manager decision citing independent review REVIEW-14051: the operator already decided 2026-09-24 (PI-20260922-E41-0004, killed as a decision, "non-zero measurements mean their zero test does not reach these legs") to KEEP this exact arm on this exact leg, and this PR brought no new information. This corrects a claim in this lane's own prior report to the manager (which described #14051 as still HELD/open and cited it as resolving the real-money-tier survey's last open cell) -- that claim was stale, made from context that predated the closure. The SUBSTANTIVE conclusion (no new real-money-tier work open) is unaffected: xrp_pullback_2h/trail_decay is settled as a KEEP, not stripped. || PRECISE ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-29 (same check-in): un-drafting alone did NOT explain the stuck state, and "any fresh push" was too vague -- actually confirmed via `mcp__github__actions_list` (list_workflow_runs filtered to the branch) that claude-pr-automerge.yml's `push` trigger carries `paths: ['.github/pr-automerge-requests/*.txt']` (not just `branches: ["claude/**"]`, which is all this record's own `what` field quoted). #14299's post-un-draft push (60bc65bb, a pipeline-record-only commit) touched nothing under that path, so the workflow never even triggered -- confirmed by listing its workflow runs for that branch: only ONE run existed, from the original PR-open push, for over 30 minutes after the un-draft. #14322's post-un-draft push happened to be a `git merge origin/main`, which incidentally pulled in OTHER lanes' new `.github/pr-automerge-requests/*.txt` files and so matched the filter by coincidence, not by design -- which is why it worked and #14299's did not, despite both following the same un-draft+push recipe. Fixed by merging origin/main into #14299 a second time (confirmed via `git show --stat` that the merge commit's diff touched the path before pushing); the workflow then ran and logged "auto-merge enabled on #14299". CORRECTED PROCEDURE for any future stuck self-land PR: after un-drafting, the retriggering push must touch a file under .github/pr-automerge-requests/ -- merging main is the simplest way to do that reliably, but confirm the merge commit's diff actually includes such a file (git show --stat -- .github/pr-automerge-requests/) before assuming the merge alone unblocks it, since a merge with nothing new under that path would silently not help.
